[EFFECT]
Temperature has a non-monotonic (inverted-U shaped) effect on hourly bike demand. Very cold hours (near 0°C) strongly suppress predicted rentals — the model's contribution is around –0.8 to –0.9 in log space, meaning far fewer bikes are expected. Demand rises steeply as temperatures climb, reaching its peak positive contribution (roughly +0.2 to +0.3) at around 25–31°C (normalised temp ≈ 0.65–0.75). Beyond that sweet spot, the contribution declines again, and at the highest temperatures (above roughly 33°C) the effect turns negative, meaning extremely hot hours also dampen demand.

[IMPORTANCE]
Temperature is the **3rd most important feature** in the model, with an importance score of 0.197 — closely behind the year indicator (0.200) and far behind the hour of day (0.833), which dominates all other features. Compared to the remaining six features (weekday, month, humidity, weather situation, wind speed, and holiday), temperature is meaningfully more influential.

[RECOMMENDATION]
Plan for peak bike availability and staffing during mild-to-warm weather (roughly 25–31°C), as those are the hours the model expects the highest demand; conversely, you can scale back resources during cold winter days and during unusually hot heatwaves, when ridership is predicted to drop significantly.
